title: Ranger bow retained local geometry focused evidence
conclusion: When exact local draw point and flex are unchanged, retaining bowstring geometry and cached limb nodes preserves reviewed output and reduces the complete equipped-bow update_pose callback by about 40-46% in the focused repeated-pose workload.

sourceBasis.postRunNormalization: The frozen bow fixture final file removes one trailing blank line and the probe updates that file-hash constant. The frozen pose function bytes and runtime semantics are unchanged; per-session manifests retain the exact measured file hashes.

correctness.windowedExactParity: 19 actor presentation states plus 11-step dynamic bow sequence; zero failures
dynamicCases: idle world motion with retained local geometry

rejectedAttempts.reason: invalid post-timing state comparison and diagnostic iteration; excluded
snapshot included autogenerated node names; excluded
test reset cleared retained string without invalidating cache; excluded

limitations: Focused callback timings repeatedly invoke update_pose at a stable sampled animation time; they include called engine APIs and mesh submission but exclude skeleton evaluation, signal dispatch, GPU work, and whole-frame pacing.
The retained fast path applies only when exact local draw point and flex are unchanged. Advancing draw or recoil poses rebuild geometry.
Windowed exact mesh and pose parity was established with Compatibility rendering. Forward+ and whole-scene frame-rate effects were not measured in this focused bundle.
Unchanged melee, casting, and unequipped-idle timing differences are measurement noise and are not attributed to this bow-only patch.
